subsystems.name: Field sampling
subsystems.role: gets uncontaminated material out of hostile environments (deep sea, ice, rock, acid).

subsystems.name: Containment and culture
subsystems.role: grows organisms under the same extreme conditions they came from, which is often required before any lab work can begin.
parts: high-pressure bioreactors (up to hundreds of bar)
radiation exposure rigs up to thousands of gray

subsystems.name: Sequencing and molecular analysis
subsystems.role: identifies what is there and how it survives when most of it cannot be cultured.

subsystems.name: Analogue site access
subsystems.role: provides Earth environments that stand in for Mars, Europa or Enceladus.

subsystems.name: Life-detection instrument development
subsystems.role: turns what extremophiles taught us into instruments light and tough enough to fly.

subsystems.name: Data and biosignature modelling
subsystems.role: decides which chemical or morphological signals would actually count as evidence of life.

buildSteps.title: Pick the analogue
buildSteps.detail: Choose an Earth site whose temperature, pressure, salinity, radiation or chemistry matches the target world — a vent field for Europa, a permafrost borehole for Mars.

buildSteps.title: Survey and map
buildSteps.detail: Sample the physical setting first: chemistry, temperature gradients, mineralogy and radiation dose, so that any organism found can be tied to its exact conditions.

buildSteps.title: Sample cleanly
buildSteps.detail: Use sterilised tools and sealed containers, with blanks and controls, so that what is sequenced later can be shown to come from the site and not from the ship or the lab.

buildSteps.title: Preserve and transport
buildSteps.detail: Split each sample: part frozen or chemically fixed for sequencing, part kept alive under pressure or in anaerobic conditions for culturing.

buildSteps.title: Culture and isolate
buildSteps.detail: Grow organisms at the site's temperature, pressure, pH and salt level. Most resist culturing, so this often takes years and specific media.

buildSteps.title: Sequence and compare
buildSteps.detail: Reconstruct genomes from mixed samples, identify the organisms and look for the genes and proteins that explain survival — for example DNA repair or unusual membrane chemistry.

buildSteps.title: Test the mechanism
buildSteps.detail: Recreate the stress in the lab (radiation, freeze-thaw, vacuum, desiccation) and measure whether the proposed survival mechanism actually protects cells.

buildSteps.title: Set the limits of life
buildSteps.detail: Publish the measured envelope — the maximum temperature, pressure, radiation dose or dryness at which growth is still observed.

buildSteps.title: Feed it into mission design
buildSteps.detail: Convert those limits into instrument sensitivity targets, sampling depths and contamination rules for spacecraft heading to Mars, Europa or Enceladus.

prerequisites.why: environmental samples contain very little DNA and are easily swamped by contamination; detecting it reliably is the foundation of the whole field.
many extremophiles only grow under conditions that ordinary lab vessels cannot maintain.
drilling into subglacial lakes without contaminating them is hard, slow and done only a handful of times.
instruments must survive launch, vacuum and radiation while detecting molecules at very low concentration.
rules limiting how clean a spacecraft must be are what make a claimed detection believable.

pathway.milestone: a growing catalogue of organisms with measured survival limits, plus a good understanding of contamination
pathway.unlocks: informed choices about which Martian or icy-moon sites are worth visiting.

pathway.milestone: sample-return missions such as Mars Sample Return, with samples studied in terrestrial labs
pathway.unlocks: far more sensitive analysis than any rover can carry.

pathway.milestone: dedicated life-detection payloads on Europa and Enceladus missions
pathway.unlocks: direct tests of whether subsurface oceans are habitable.

pathway.milestone: clean subsurface access to an ocean world, or returned plume material
pathway.unlocks: the first real chance to distinguish a habitable environment from an inhabited one.
